{{Italic title}}
'''''This Book Needs No Title: A Budget of Living Paradoxes''''' is a 1980 collection of essays about [[logic]], [[paradox]]es, and [[philosophy]], by [[Raymond Smullyan]]. It was first published by [[Prentice-Hall]].

In 2023, it was reissued by What Is the Name of This Press, with a new foreword by [[Donald Knuth]].<ref name="What">[https://raymondsmullyan.com/books/this-book-needs-no-title/ This Book Needs No Title], retrieved Mar 2, 2023</ref>

==Reception==

''[[Kirkus Reviews]]'' called it "funny" and "provocative", commending Smullyan's descriptions of [[Zen]] and noting that the book could appeal to both children and adults, but conceded that Smullyan's work may be an "[[acquired taste]]".<ref name=Kirkus>[https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/raymond-smullyan-3/this-book-needs-no-title-a-budget-of-living-par/ THIS BOOK NEEDS NO TITLE: A Budget of Living Paradoxes], reviewed at ''[[Kirkus Reviews]]''; published May 7, 1980; retrieved May 27, 2018</ref>

''[[The Washington Post]]'' has described "This Book Needs No Title" as "tantalizing",<ref name=WaPo>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/entertainment/books/1997/07/27/hardcovers-in-brief/05c45a88-39d8-4566-ae28-fdf94c49ba1b/ HARDCOVERS IN BRIEF], reviewed at ''[[the Washington Post]]''; published July 27, 1997; retrieved May 27, 2018</ref> while [[Michael Dirda]] has declared that (along with Smullyan's earlier "What is the Name of this Book") it has "the cleverest of all titles", positing that Smullyan may have been inspired by [[Denis Diderot]]'s "[[Ceci n'est pas un conte]]".<ref name=Dirda>[https://theamericanscholar.org/this-is-a-column This Is a Column], by [[Michael Dirda]], in ''[[The American Scholar (magazine)|The American Scholar]]''; published March 16, 2012; retrieved May 27, 2012</ref>
